Tendon count is the discrete group and routing is the continuous group. Segment count and span strategy remain fixed to avoid confounding backbone topology; lengths, materials, sections, and payout remain fixed so the three evaluations focus on constraint coverage and route geometry. One load permits three distinct structures within the three-evaluation cap. The finite intervals are local-to-moderate test bounds only and do not close the full FamilySpace.
plan.stopping_condition: Stop after at most six proposals and at most three static condition-analysis entries, or earlier if the admitted bounded proposals are exhausted. Then read the actual saved search result and assess evaluated candidates, actual parameter changes, qualification or failure, the best mathematical candidate if any, unexplored scope, and unmeasured full-task acceptance. Do not run additional physics.
plan.weakening_observation: No evaluated proposal qualifies under s3_positive, or the finite search fails to exercise both tendon count and routing. Qualification only for the unchanged three-tendon initial routing would also weaken the claim that the qualified branch is robust to mixed structural changes.

decision.selected_method: bounded passive mixed-coordinate static-equilibrium screening closeout

plan.expected_observation: The finite search should exercise both the discrete tendon-count choice and a continuous routing coordinate, with at least one evaluated proposal passing the complete s3_positive static equilibrium qualification with finite residuals, positive reduced stiffness, and tendon tensions within capacity.
plan.fixed_conditions: Base-only passive soft structures; unilateral tendons; fixed assembly payout semantics; no active control; two segments; whole-chain spans; the frozen native model and passive re-equilibrated static method; diagnostic load s3_positive only; finite authorized tendon counts 3 or 4 and routing bounds anchor_s [0.75,1.0], angular_offset_rad [-0.35,0.35], guide_s [0.3,0.7], phase_rad [-0.35,0.35], and radius_m [0.012,0.022]. Lengths, materials, sections, payout, span strategy, other load conditions, dynamics, and task evaluator were held fixed or unmeasured.
plan.hypothesis: Within the authorized two-segment, three-or-four-tendon fixed-payout passive family, changing tendon count and bounded routing coordinates can preserve a contact-free, capacity-respecting, locally stable, strictly complementary equilibrium under the s3_positive diagnostic load; this is a static qualification hypothesis, not a full-task-performance claim.
plan.interpretation: The initial diagnostic result_1 established only a qualified unloaded local equilibrium for candidate_19. The completed finite search then legally constructed and evaluated three designs. Candidate_271 used the authorized family defaults with two segments and three tendons; it qualified under s3_positive with score -0.9992419266704128. Candidate_280 changed the discrete tendon_count from 3 to 4 and also qualified, with score -0.9995131110458512. Candidate_289 retained four tendons and changed the continuous coordinate routing.phase_rad; it qualified under the same loaded-condition screen with score -0.9999279283119049, loaded-condition LICQ and strict complementarity true, reduced stiffness about 0.19053 N m/rad, maximum tendon tension about 0.0320 N, zero primal violation, and stationarity about 7.21e-11 N m. Thus both a discrete and a continuous move were actually exercised, all three loaded-condition analyses qualified, and candidate_289 is the best mathematical candidate under the stated score. This supports the narrow finite-search hypothesis that qualification can persist across the tested topology/routing changes. It does not show task improvement: the objective was the worst dimensionless KKT qualification residual, not any displacement constraint or full-task score. Moreover, candidate_289's separate unloaded multistart summary includes a selected working point lacking LICQ and strict complementarity, so no broader robustness claim is made from the loaded-condition ranking. The search examined only three points, one load condition, tendon counts 3 and 4, and one recorded continuous phase move after initialization. Segment count 3, alternative spans, lengths, materials, sections, payout, most routing combinations, opposite loads, and the remaining frozen conditions were unexplored. Complete dynamics, independent Replay, and original ten-condition task acceptance remain unmeasured. Remaining legal scientific alternatives would ordinarily include a broader static search over those groups or full finite-time task validation, but both are outside the completed authorized mathematical allowance here; physical budget is zero, protected closeout is active, and the operator explicitly requires ending after this assessment with no extra physics. Continuing would therefore be unauthorized and would not improve evidence within this invocation. The fresh-result index contains result_1, result_2, result_3, and result_4; all are cited above, and none supplies independent task acceptance.
plan.stopping_condition: Stop after the authorized search uses its three mathematical evaluations or six-proposal ceiling, then report the actual evaluated moves and limitations without starting dynamics or further physics. The search terminated because its three-evaluation budget was exhausted, satisfying this condition.
plan.weakening_observation: The hypothesis would be weakened if no evaluated proposal qualified under s3_positive, if the search failed to exercise both tendon count and routing, or if qualification occurred only for the unchanged initial three-tendon routing.

interpretations.text: The frozen passive, unloaded local mechanism produced two converged qualified-local-minimum trials, requiring 14 and 70 optimizer iterations.
